video_title: Why Power Trading Is 10X Crazier Than Crypto ft. Cory Paddock | Open Interest | Ep.24
gist: Cory Paddock, co-founder of Calgary-based prop power-trading firm GBE Energy, explains how PJM electricity futures (chiefly PJM West Hub balance-of-day on ICE) are traded intraday on load/generation/transmission mismatches, with volatility he calls '10x crypto'. Key edges: power must physically clear within hours so fundamental views get validated fast; a structural short-risk-premium strategy punctuated by sized longs on 'booby trap' tail days; and a current supply-demand squeeze in PJM from data-center load arriving while plants retire. He also describes building traders from young recruits in 6-8 months, helped by LLM fluency.

insights.claim: North America's grid is three largely separate machines — the Western, Eastern and Texas (ERCOT) interconnections — with almost no AC links and only a few DC ties between them, so power prices in Texas can diverge substantially from those in New York.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Regional power prices are not arbitrageable across interconnections; treat each as a separate market for price and data-center siting risk.

insights.claim: PJM, spanning New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia, Ohio and metro Chicago, is the largest deregulated power market in the world and the most liquid in the Eastern Interconnection.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: PJM is the bellwether US power market for data-center-driven price dynamics.
insights.quote: it's the biggest deregulated power market in the world

insights.claim: PJM's rough generation mix is about 40% natural gas, 15-20% coal, 20% nuclear, with wind and solar making up the rest and a little oil, after a shale-driven coal-to-gas switch that began about 10 years ago using cheap Marcellus gas from western Pennsylvania.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: PJM power prices remain heavily tied to Marcellus gas prices, linking power and natural gas trades.

insights.claim: Power market design is a response to what the region's generation technologies can do, and system operators always tip the balance toward reliability over minimizing production cost.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Operator reliability actions (out-of-market dispatch, conservative commitments) are a persistent source of price surprises traders must model.
insights.quote: always um the scales are going to be tipped towards reliability

insights.claim: Although PJM remains summer-peaking due to air-conditioning load, some PJM sub-zones are transitioning to winter-peaking as heating demand exceeds summer AC demand.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Winter becomes a new tail-risk season for PJM price spikes; seasonal risk premia may be mispriced by participants anchored to summer peaks.

insights.claim: Paddock says the bipartisan political coalition that created deregulated, optimization-based US power markets in the 1980s-2000s would be almost impossible to assemble in today's political environment.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Major market-design reforms are unlikely; expect incremental rule changes rather than new unified markets.

insights.claim: GBE Energy trades mostly PJM West Hub futures on ICE, a hub of nodes spread across western Pennsylvania and the Washington DC area that serves as the benchmark for PJM power prices.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: PJM West Hub on ICE is the primary liquid instrument for expressing a view on PJM power.

insights.claim: Unlike North American gas, PJM power futures offer granularity down to balance-of-week, next-day and balance-of-day contracts; the balance-of-day contract settles on the weighted average of five-minute nodal prices from hour-ending 8 to 23 on business days, so part of the settlement is known intraday while the remainder can still swing.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Balance-of-day contracts let traders express intraday fundamental views with partial information, a distinctive edge versus other energy futures.

insights.claim: Even 24 hours ahead, with modern weather forecasts, traders do not really know how power will flow on the grid the next day, and fundamentals can change substantially in that window.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Day-ahead power prices embed genuine uncertainty that skilled fundamental traders can monetize.
insights.quote: you would think that we know how uh the grid is going to behave tomorrow um when we're only 24 hours out but it turns out actually no

insights.claim: Options on PJM power futures are thin: there are some monthly options, while balance-of-day and next-day options liquidity has dried up over the past several years.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Limited options markets mean tail risk must be managed via futures sizing and stops, not bought protection.

insights.claim: New exchange Electron X, which GBE Energy joined weeks ago, lists each individual hour as a separate power futures contract, and Paddock forecasts many participants will adopt it because load-serving entities and renewables with non-flat shapes can hedge only select hours.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Hourly power futures could draw renewables-hedging volume away from ICE strip contracts; watch Electron X liquidity growth.

insights.claim: ICE closes power trading at 6 PM daily for server maintenance, leaving unsettled hours at day's end, and GBE Energy typically carries open positions into delivery and across the next several days.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Overnight gap risk from the ICE close is a structural feature of PJM futures exposure.

insights.claim: GBE Energy's average holding period is roughly 10-12 hours or less, making it predominantly an intraday business with occasional two-to-three-day positions.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Power alpha is short-horizon; allocators should evaluate power prop/hedge funds as intraday discretionary strategies.

insights.claim: GBE Energy's core process is a daily checklist forecasting load by sub-region, which generators are on or off, and whether transmission can move cheap generation into high-load pockets; the price of the next megawatt once transmission hits its limit determines whether futures are too high or too low.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: A reusable framework for power price calls: load vs. deliverable supply, with transmission congestion setting marginal prices.

insights.claim: Paddock says understanding load extremely well comes first and most of GBE Energy's trades are downstream of load forecasts, which vary by sub-region, season, time of day and sun angle.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Load forecasting skill, not generation data, is the primary alpha source in PJM power.

insights.claim: Proprietary vendors monitor power-plant output in real time using sensors typically placed in farmers' fields that measure flow on high-voltage lines leaving generators, supplementing public ISO data and NOAA GFS and European weather models.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Real-time generation alt-data is a paid edge in power trading; weather data itself is public and the edge is in converting it to load.
insights.quote: they do this through some sensors that are located typically in farmers fields

insights.claim: Power markets are very data-rich, and GBE Energy has always stored all ISO and vendor data even without knowing its future use, an approach Paddock says has recently been validated internally.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Proprietary historical datasets are becoming a moat as ML/LLM tooling makes old data exploitable.

insights.claim: Power is uniquely rewarding for fundamental traders because power must physically flow and the lights must stay on, so a correct view is validated within hours rather than the weeks or years it may take in other markets, making it hard to get bullied out of a well-founded position.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Short convergence horizons make power an attractive venue for discretionary fundamental alpha versus markets where mispricings persist.
insights.quote: ultimately the power has to flow, the lights have to stay on and so um you just have to have the patience of a number of hours to to see if your your market view is right

insights.claim: Paddock argues PJM contracts are addictive and liquid partly because they mix skill and chance like well-designed games: just when a trader thinks they've solved it, randomness intervenes.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Explains persistent speculative participation that supplies liquidity and risk premium in PJM.

insights.claim: Opacity and limited access to PJM power markets make them alpha-rich enough for a prop trading business to thrive, per Paddock's agreement with host Moritz Seibert.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Niche, hard-to-access commodity markets retain alpha that crowded markets lose.

insights.claim: Paddock describes PJM power volatility as roughly '10x crypto', measured not just day-to-day but in how prices whip between consecutive five-minute intervals.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Position sizing in power must assume extreme intraday moves; standard vol-targeting from other commodities understates risk.
insights.quote: 10x crypto I think is probably the the best way to describe it

insights.claim: Stop-losses remain necessary in power trading, but slippage when prices get high can be extraordinary, so short positions must be sized for both where the contract can trade intraday and where it can ultimately settle.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Short power exposure carries gap/settlement risk that stops cannot fully contain; size shorts to worst-case settlement.

insights.claim: Paddock's 'four stages of power trading': (1) always long chasing tail spikes and bleeding, (2) always short until a tail day wipes out profits, (3) short most days while avoiding 'booby trap' long days, and (4) the actualized stage — short most of the time to harvest the risk premium and pivoting long on the tail days, which produce most of the year's gains.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Power prices embed a persistent tail-risk premium; the optimal strategy is short carry plus opportunistic, well-sized long convexity on identifiable spike days.
insights.quote: a lot of the time you're short um because market participants want to pay for that tail risk and then on the booby trap days you actually pivot and you're long

insights.claim: Sizing the long on tail days is the art of power trading: getting enough size requires enough participants to disagree with you, which usually means tolerating a meaningful mark-to-market drawdown before the payoff.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Expect big wins to follow painful drawdowns; conviction sizing against consensus is the source of outsized P&L.
insights.quote: to go and initiate a trade against the rest of the market and get enough size you're going to need enough people to disagree with you

insights.claim: Retail power products (Paddock and host recall an older bank ETN on US power and a more recent ETF) that are passively long power may be poorly designed because power usually carries a risk premium that rewards being short — unless the market is in a new paradigm shift, which Paddock thinks may be halfway underway.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Be skeptical of passive long-power ETFs as AI-power plays; the roll/risk premium works against them except in structural shortage regimes.
insights.quote: Unless you get into this new paradigm shift which I feel like we might be halfway in into.

insights.claim: An enormous wave of data-center demand entered the PJM footprint just as many generator retirements were still happening, and that overlap was not seamless, pushing PJM into more frequent very high-price power days.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Supports a tighter-for-longer PJM supply outlook, bullish for PJM power prices, capacity values and generation owners in the region.
insights.quote: there's an enormous amount of um of data center demand on in that's entered into uh into the footprint just at the moment in time where a bunch of retirements were still happening

insights.claim: The mismatch between generation investment and load growth in PJM will not resolve in a matter of months; Paddock expects it to resolve over the coming years, timing unclear.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Multi-year window of elevated PJM volatility and price spikes before new supply catches up.

insights.claim: Paddock sees power as the best commodity to be in for the next 10 years because data-center buildout, vehicle electrification and electrification of heat and buildings plus added air conditioning will all happen; the only question is speed, with oversupply and undersupply cycles along the way.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Structural electricity demand growth underpins long-term bullishness on power infrastructure, but expect commodity-style boom/bust cycles.
insights.quote: largely speaking there's not a better commodity to be in

insights.claim: Participation in power markets has grown more slowly over the past 10 years than Paddock expected, and because no market design has fully solved the physics-plus-economics problem, power may remain a set of insular, idiosyncratic regional pockets rather than a globally liquid market.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Alpha in power may persist because fragmentation limits institutional crowding.

insights.claim: Paddock's biggest career trades came from paradigm shifts that change grid topology; before the market, load, generators and system operators adapt, there is a burst of mispricing and volatility.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Watch for structural grid changes (zone integrations, large plant retirements, new transmission) as the highest-payoff setups in power.

insights.claim: When portions of Ohio moved from the Midwest ISO into PJM, a view on those zones' supply-demand balance produced six days one summer that made up about 85% of that year's P&L and seeded the capital to start GBE Energy.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Illustrates how concentrated power-trading returns are around structural events.
insights.quote: there was six days um that summer uh that made up, you know, kind of 85% of our P&L that year

insights.claim: Paddock's worst loss came from staying short against a very specific transmission constraint, betting the macro picture would win, and exiting too late — a lesson that local transmission constraints can override broad supply-demand views.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: In nodal power markets, local congestion can dominate macro fundamentals; respect constraint-driven price risk.

themes.theme: Building traders in the LLM era

insights.claim: GBE Energy shifted from backing experienced traders to developing young, hungry recruits, inspired by partner firm Greenwich Commodities, which trades financial transmission rights and grew interns into full traders.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Talent pipelines, not just capital, are becoming the constraint and competitive moat in niche commodity trading.

insights.claim: GBE Energy expected new analysts to need 16-18 months (a full seasonal cycle) before making useful calls, but its most recent recruits were ready to deploy capital in 6-8 months.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Faster trader ramp-up lowers the cost of scaling discretionary commodity trading desks.

insights.claim: Traders under 25 who are fluent with LLMs can build models and tools extraordinarily fast, though they still need a firm's tacit context to 'bully the LLMs into the right answer'.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: LLMs compress analyst development time but proprietary domain context remains the moat.
insights.quote: you still need to know uh and bully the LLMs into the right answer

insights.claim: GBE Energy offers traders near-certainty on compensation, contrasting with discretionary bonuses at larger firms, which Paddock identifies as one of a trader's biggest stresses.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: Formulaic payout structures are a recruiting edge for prop firms competing with banks and large trading houses.

insights.claim: Paddock screens recruits for a demonstrated, unteachable will to trade and take risk — trading their own accounts, building models, sports betting or online poker — rather than prior power-market knowledge.
insights.speaker: Cory Paddock
insights.so_what: A hiring framework for discretionary trading: risk appetite is innate, domain knowledge is teachable.
